headline: Custom Interior Remodeling: What to Prepare Before Demolition Begins
articleBody:
Starting a custom interior remodel can feel like a whirlwind, and it's easy to jump straight into picking out new finishes. But before any sledgehammers come out, there are some crucial steps to take to ensure your project goes smoothly. Getting these ducks in a row early on will save you a lot of headaches, unexpected costs, and delays down the line.

First up, solidify your design. Have all your layouts, drawings, and finish selections completely decided and documented. Changing your mind mid-demolition can halt progress and introduce expensive revisions. Next, ensure your project's scope is crystal clear. This means knowing exactly what will be demolished, what stays, and what new elements are going in. This clarity helps prevent misunderstandings and ensures everyone is on the same page.

Next, confirm all necessary permits are secured. Depending on your project's scope—especially if it involves structural changes, electrical work, or plumbing relocation—you'll likely need permits from your local jurisdiction. LineWork Development coordinates this as part of an integrated design-build process, but if you're managing parts yourself, it’s vital to get this done. Without permits, you risk fines and having to redo work. Finally, think about how the work will affect your daily life. Can you remain in your home? What areas will be off-limits? Making arrangements for temporary living spaces or planning daily routines around construction zones will make the process much smoother.

What to Prepare Before You Start:

Before demolition day arrives, gather all finalized architectural drawings and plans, confirm your material orders are placed and ideally on-site or scheduled for timely delivery, and make sure all necessary permits have been officially issued and posted. It's also smart to protect adjacent areas of your home that won't be under renovation; think about dust barriers, floor coverings, and moving furniture out of the way. Having a clear plan for trash and debris removal will also keep your site organized and safe. This preparation allows the build team to start strong and maintain momentum, reducing overall project duration.
